# Results — Study 851 (Netflix Password Crackdown)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Netflix's 2023 paid-sharing ("password crackdown"), feared to spike churn, became an
**upside surprise**: a single-name news-reaction event study of NFLX's abnormal returns
around the five public dates of the story. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped), i.e. as-of 2026-06-30.
Fingerprint `5fff2e717a0c` (NFLX Close; SPY `da459bd64b22`, QQQ `f8f1d5c5542a`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **NFLX, SPY, QQQ**, 2015-01-02 → 2026-06-30, **2,889** rows/name, cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Event calendar | **5 hardcoded public dates** of the paid-sharing story (2022-04-20 → 2023-10-19), from the Netflix quarterly shareholder letters / newsroom — matters of public record (`data.EVENTS`, each row sourced) |
| Abnormal return | **one-factor market model**: OLS α/β on a **120-session estimation window ending 10 sessions before** the event window (strictly out-of-sample); AR = `r_NFLX − (α + β·r_mkt)`. SPY is the headline benchmark; QQQ a cross-check |
| Event window | `[−1..+5]` sessions; day 0 = the first session that could trade the news. **Execution lag:** Netflix reports after the close, so an earnings reaction lands on the **next** session (encoded in the calendar — zero look-ahead) |
| Statistics | cross-event one-sample *t* (n=5, **4 df — fat tails**); Wilson hit-rate interval; a **4,000-draw random-calendar placebo**; an event-bootstrap CI; a leave-one-out cut; a 20-seed synthetic control on 30 pseudo-events |
| Trade (timer) | long-only: buy NFLX at the event-session close, hold N sessions; one round trip of one-way cost × NAV charged twice; no borrow |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** NFLX is a single, continuously-listed name
over the whole window (no cross-sectional survivor screen), so survivorship is not the
threat here; the binding limitation is **N = 5 events → almost no statistical power**.
This is a **case study**, not a factor — the value is the anatomy, not a *t*-stat.

## The headline — cross-event mean event-session abnormal return (vs SPY)

Per-event day-0 abnormal NFLX return (market model), the five dates that *are* the story:

| react session | event | raw NFLX | abnormal (vs SPY) | est. β |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2022-04-20 | Q1'22 letter first flags paid-sharing (sub miss) | −35.12% | **−34.55%** | 1.60 |
| 2022-08-22 | LatAm 'add-a-home' paid-sharing test | −6.06% | −2.34% | 1.66 |
| 2023-05-23 | broad US paid-sharing rollout | −1.93% | −0.34% | 1.50 |
| 2023-07-20 | Q2'23 letter: +5.9M subs (revenue miss) | −8.41% | −7.64% | 1.37 |
| 2023-10-19 | Q3'23 letter: +8.8M subs — the payoff | +16.05% | **+17.34%** | 1.55 |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **cross-event mean day-0 abnormal return** | **−5.51%** |
| one-sample *t* (n=5, 4 df) | **−0.66** |
| up-days | **1 / 5** (Wilson 95% [4%, 62%]) |
| event-bootstrap 95% CI on the mean | **[−21.7%, +8.4%]** |
| whole-window CAR [−1..+5] | −4.01% (*t* = −0.38) |
| post-event CAR [+1..+5] | +1.39% (*t* = +0.45) |
| cross-check vs QQQ (day-0 mean) | −4.79% (*t* = −0.59) |

The claimed **upside surprise does not show up as a tradable abnormal-return signal**.
The cross-event average is actually *negative* — but that is entirely the single
**2022-04-20** announcement crash (Netflix flagged the policy in the same letter that
reported its first subscriber decline in a decade), not a downside edge. The promised
upside is a **single event** (Q3'23, +17.34% abnormal). The bootstrap CI straddles zero
by ±20 points. With n=5 there is no power in either direction.

## Placebo — is five real dates unlike five random ones?

Same market-model statistic on 4,000 random 5-date calendars drawn from the interior of
the tape:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed 5-event mean | **−5.51%** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.01% (1.07%) |
| right-tail p (≥ observed) | 0.998 |
| left-tail p (≤ observed) | **0.003** |

The observed mean sits in the **left** tail — the *wrong* side for an "upside surprise",
and an artifact of one −35% outlier dominating a five-point average. It is **not**
evidence of a downside signal; it is the fingerprint of a sample too small to average.

## Robustness — the whole result is one date

| cut | n | mean day-0 AR | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| all events | 5 | −5.51% | −0.66 |
| **drop the 2022-04 crash** | 4 | **+1.75%** | +0.32 |
| confirmation earnings only (Q2+Q3'23) | 2 | +4.85% | +0.39 |

Remove the single 2022-04 announcement crash and the mean flips to ≈0. Even the
confirmation earnings alone — where the "it worked" narrative lives — are only mildly
positive and utterly powerless at n=2. Every cut says the same thing: **too few events.**

## The timer — could you have traded it?

Long NFLX from the event-session close, held N sessions; one round trip of one-way cost
× NAV charged twice; vs the unconditional NFLX N-day baseline.

| hold | gross | net (10 bps) | *t* (net) | win-rate | uncond. NFLX |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d | −87.7 bps | −107.7 bps | −1.06 | 20% | +12.9 bps |
| 3d | +65.4 bps | +45.4 bps | +0.19 | 60% | +39.6 bps |
| 5d | −231.9 bps | −251.9 bps | −0.56 | 40% | +66.6 bps |
| 10d | +62.7 bps | +42.7 bps | +0.11 | 40% | +134.0 bps |
| 21d | +264.7 bps | +244.7 bps | +0.34 | 60% | +277.0 bps |

The net buy-the-event return swings wildly with the holding period, never with a *t* far
from zero, and never a clean win over simply holding NFLX. No edge to charge costs
against. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic one-factor tape (`r_asset = drift + β·r_mkt + idio`, β≈1.25) with a TUNABLE
planted one-day abnormal jump on **30** scheduled pseudo-events (30, not 5, so the
small-N fat tails don't muddy the calibration read). No network.

| world | day-0 mean AR / *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean *t* **+0.37** (sd 1.06), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.03`, seed 851) | mean **+2.86%**, *t* = **+11.12** |

The detector is well-calibrated (null centred at ≈0, ~5% crossings) and recovers a
planted jump cleanly. The real-tape emptiness is therefore a genuine **sample-size**
verdict, not a broken or asleep detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The cross-event mean event-session abnormal return is **−5.51%**
  (one-sample *t* = **−0.66**, n=5), only **1/5** events up, whole-window CAR −4.01%
  (*t* = −0.38). The claimed upside surprise is a **single event** (Q3'23, +17.34%); the
  negative average is one 2022 crash (leave-one-out → +1.75%). No robust signal in either
  direction — **n=5 has no power.** The QQQ cross-check agrees (−4.79%, *t* = −0.59).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The buy-the-event overlay never reliably beats holding NFLX;
  net *t* ∈ [−1.06, +0.34] across 1/3/5/10/21-day holds, win-rates 20–60% on five trades.
- **"The scary policy that worked?"** — true as a **business fact** (subscribers grew,
  Q3'23 popped +16%), but there is **no tradable abnormal-return signal** around the
  events at n=5. A case study, not a factor.
